traceability.evidence:
Story file and traceability: - Story exists at docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md with the specified content. - Core plugin entrypoint src/index.ts is explicitly annotated with @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md and @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE / REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, tying implementation to this story.
Core plugin structure and rule registry (REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-TYPESCRIPT, Core Functionality): - src/index.ts is written in TypeScript and imports ESLint types: `import type { Rule } from "eslint";`. - RULE_NAMES constant defines all rule IDs: const RULE_NAMES = [ "require-story-annotation", "require-req-annotation", "require-branch-annotation", "valid-annotation-format", "valid-story-reference", "valid-req-reference", ] as const; - It builds a rule registry: `const rules: Record = {} as any;` and populates it by iterating RULE_NAMES and requiring `./rules/${name}`. - All referenced rule implementations exist as TypeScript modules in src/rules/: - require-story-annotation.ts - require-req-annotation.ts - require-branch-annotation.ts - valid-annotation-format.ts - valid-story-reference.ts - valid-req-reference.ts - The plugin exports are well-structured: - Named exports: `export { rules, configs, maintenance };` - Default export: `export default { rules, configs, maintenance };` - This matches standard ESLint plugin module structure and provides a clear registry for multiple rules.
Config system and ESLint v9 flat-config integration (REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT, REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM, Integration): - src/index.ts defines `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` mapping full rule names (e.g. "traceability/require-story-annotation") to severities ("error" or "warn"). - Function `createTraceabilityFlatConfig()` returns an ESLint v9 flat-config style object: { plugins: { traceability: {} }, rules: { ...TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES }, } - `configs` is defined as: const configs = { recommended: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], strict: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], }; which matches ESLint v9 flat config expectations for plugin presets. - The project has a real flat ESLint config wired to this plugin at the root in eslint.config.js: - Uses @eslint/js and @typescript-eslint/parser. - Dynamically loads the plugin from ./src/index.js or ./lib/src/index.js and, when present, registers it via the `plugins` field in flat config: plugins: { ...(plugin.rules ? { traceability: plugin } : {}) }. - Applies that plugin both to TypeScript and JavaScript file configs. - Integration tests invoke ESLint 9 CLI with this flat config and the plugin, confirming that the config and plugin work together, not just in theory.
Error handling for rule loading and plugin usage (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, Acceptance Criteria: Error Handling): - src/index.ts wraps dynamic rule loading in a try/catch for each RULE_NAMES entry: try { const mod = require(`./rules/${name}`); rules[name] = mod.default ?? mod; } catch (error: any) { console.error(`[eslint-plugin-traceability] Failed to load rule "${name}": ${error.message}`); rules[name] = { ...placeholder RuleModule ... }; } - The placeholder RuleModule has: - meta.docs.description: `Failed to load rule '${name}'`. - create(context) that reports on Program with the message: `eslint-plugin-traceability: Error loading rule "${name}": ${error.message}`. - tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts (header references this story and REQ-ERROR-HANDLING) verifies: - A mocked rule module (require-branch-annotation) throws on import. - Requiring ../src/index triggers the error path. - console.error is called with a message containing `Failed to load rule "require-branch-annotation": Test load error`. - plugin.rules["require-branch-annotation"] is defined. - meta.docs.description for the placeholder rule contains `Failed to load rule 'require-branch-annotation'`. - The placeholder rule’s Program visitor reports an error containing `Error loading rule "require-branch-annotation": Test load error`. - tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts (also tagged with this story and REQ-ERROR-HANDLING) invokes the real ESLint CLI via spawnSync using eslint.config.js and: - Asserts non-zero exit when required rule detects missing annotations. - Asserts that stdout includes the expected, descriptive error message about missing @story annotations. - These tests confirm graceful handling of rule-load failures and clear user feedback at both plugin and CLI levels, satisfying the story’s Error Handling acceptance criterion (marked [x] in the story).
Plugin registration, default export, and configs validated by tests (REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM, Quality Standards): - tests/plugin-setup.test.ts: - Header: `@story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md`, `@req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - plugin exports rules and configs`. - Imports plugin, { rules, configs } from "../src/index". - Asserts: - `rules` and `configs` are defined and objects. - Default export mirrors named exports: `expect(plugin.rules).toBe(rules); expect(plugin.configs).toBe(configs);`. - Confirms core plugin structure and registration. - tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts: - Header includes this story plus Story 007.0; it tests both plugin structure and error-severity mapping. - Validates default export contains rules and configs. - Validates rule registry names precisely match the RULE_NAMES array: - Expected: ["require-story-annotation", "require-req-annotation", "require-branch-annotation", "valid-annotation-format", "valid-story-reference", "valid-req-reference"]. - Verifies configs.recommended[0].rules has the correct mapping: - All core traceability rules present. - valid-annotation-format is "warn" and the others are "error". - Verifies configs.strict[0].rules equals configs.recommended[0].rules. - These tests confirm REQ-RULE-REGISTRY and REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM are implemented, and that the plugin exposes correct presets in a manner consistent with ESLint best practices.
ESLint v9 CLI integration tests (Integration, REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE): - tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts: - Header: `@story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md`, `@req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - Validate plugin registers via CLI`. - Resolves ESLint CLI from the installed eslint dev dependency and uses the project’s eslint.config.js. - Uses a helper runEslint that: - Passes `--no-config-lookup`, `--config `, `--stdin`, `--stdin-filename foo.js`. - Disables no-unused-vars and enables a specific traceability rule for each test. - Test matrix (it.each) includes: - Missing @story should cause non-zero exit for traceability/require-story-annotation. - Properly annotated function should exit 0 for traceability/require-story-annotation. - Missing @req should cause non-zero exit for traceability/require-req-annotation. - Path traversal and absolute-path scenarios should trigger errors for traceability/valid-req-reference. - Confirms that under ESLint 9 with flat config, the plugin rules load and behave as expected via the official CLI.
NPM package & TypeScript project setup (REQ-NPM-PACKAGE, REQ-TYPESCRIPT, REQ-TEST-SETUP, Quality Standards): - package.json: - name: "eslint-plugin-traceability" (standard ESLint plugin naming convention). - main: "lib/src/index.js", types: "lib/src/index.d.ts" (built outputs from TypeScript). - files: ["lib", "README.md", "LICENSE"] ensuring a minimal, clean distribution. - peerDependencies: { "eslint": "^9.0.0" }, engines: { "node": ">=18.18.0" } (aligned with ESLint 9 guidance). - scripts: - build: `tsc -p tsconfig.json`. - type-check: `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`. - lint, format:check, duplication, check:traceability, audit scripts, etc. - test: `jest --ci --bail`. - tsconfig.json: - compilerOptions target ES2020, module CommonJS, outDir lib, declaration true, strict true, etc. - include: ["src", "tests"]. - Jest config at jest.config.js: - Uses ts-jest preset. - testMatch: ["/tests/**/*.test.ts"]. - coverage thresholds and paths configured. - Header: `@req REQ-TEST-SETUP - Provide testing infrastructure for plugin`. - Test execution: - `npm test` runs `jest --ci --bail`; the tool invocation completed without error output, indicating that the full suite (including plugin-setup, error-handling, integration, and config tests) passes.
User-facing documentation and setup instructions (User Experience, Documentation acceptance criteria): - README.md: - Clearly describes the plugin and its purpose. - Provides installation steps for npm and Yarn, with prerequisites (Node.js >=18.18.0, ESLint v9+). - Shows a flat-config example using this plugin under both `plugins`+`rules` and via `traceability.configs.recommended` in Quick Start. - Lists available rules with links to docs/rules/*.md. - Includes sections on running tests, CLI integration, and plugin validation commands. - Points to user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md and user-docs/api-reference.md for deeper configuration details, giving clear, actionable setup instructions. - user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md: - Detailed ESLint 9 flat config guidance, including how to integrate this plugin (e.g. `export default [js.configs.recommended, traceability.configs.recommended];`). - Includes a full working example for a TypeScript plugin project that closely mirrors this repo. - docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md: - Developer-focused guide explaining plugin structure, meta, rules, configs, TypeScript build, and distribution, aligned with this project’s structure. - These docs together satisfy the story’s Documentation and User Experience expectations: end users and developers can install, configure, and extend the plugin with clear instructions.
Overall quality and best practices (Quality Standards acceptance criterion): - The project uses TypeScript, Jest, ESLint, Prettier, and jscpd with CI-oriented scripts (ci-verify, ci-verify:full, ci-verify:fast). - Code is organized into focused directories: src/index.ts, src/rules, src/maintenance, src/utils, tests/* (rules, integration, maintenance, config, utils). - Rule and config behavior is thoroughly covered by unit and integration tests, each tagged with @story references, including this one. - The plugin’s export shape (rules/configs/maintenance) and its integration via flat config follows modern ESLint plugin conventions.
Given this evidence, all acceptance criteria for Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP (core functionality, quality standards, integration with ESLint v9 flat config, user experience via documentation, error handling, and documentation of plugin structure/development) are implemented and verified by automated tests.
traceability.notes: The ESLint plugin foundation described in docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md is fully implemented. src/index.ts provides a TypeScript-based plugin entrypoint with a centralized rule registry, flat-config-compatible presets, and robust error handling for rule-loading failures. All referenced rules exist and are registered. The plugin is wired into an ESLint v9 flat configuration (eslint.config.js), and multiple Jest tests validate plugin exports, rule registry contents, configs, error handling behavior, and CLI integration using the actual ESLint CLI. The Jest and TypeScript setups (jest.config.js, tsconfig.json, npm scripts) provide a solid test infrastructure. User-facing README and user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md give clear installation and configuration instructions for the plugin. Test runs via `npm test` complete without reported failures. Therefore, this story’s implementation meets all its acceptance criteria and definition-of-done items.
